title: ～というと (〜to iu to)
shortExplanation: Used to provide an example or characteristic related to the topic; 'when it comes to', 'speaking of'.
longExplanation: The ～というと grammar point is used to indicate an example, characteristic, or association related to the topic being discussed. It can be translated as 'when it comes to', 'speaking of', or 'in terms of' in English.

examples.sentence: 日本料理というと、寿司が思い浮かぶ。
examples.romanization: Nihon ryouri to iu to, sushi ga omoiukabu.
examples.translation: When it comes to Japanese cuisine, sushi comes to mind.

examples.sentence: パリというと、エッフェル塔を思い出す。
examples.romanization: Pari to iu to, Efferu Tou wo omoidasu.
examples.translation: Speaking of Paris, I recall the Eiffel Tower.

examples.sentence: 夏休みというと、海に行くことが楽しみだ。
examples.romanization: Natsu yasumi to iu to, umi ni iku koto ga tanoshimi da.
examples.translation: When it comes to summer vacation, I look forward to going to the beach.

examples.sentence: 彼というと、いつも元気な人だと思う。
examples.romanization: Kare to iu to, itsumo genki na hito da to omou.
examples.translation: Speaking of him, I think he's always energetic.

title: ～というの～ (〜to iu no〜)
shortExplanation: Explain or emphasize the reason for a situation or action.
longExplanation: The ～というの〜 grammar point is used to provide an explanation or emphasize the reason for a certain situation or action. It can be translated as 'the reason is that...', or 'it's because...'.
formation: Verb-casual + というの, い-Adjective + というの, な-Adjective + だというの, Noun + だというの

examples.sentence: 遅刻したのは、電車が遅れたというのだ。
examples.romanization: Chikoku shita no wa, densha ga okureta to iu no da.
examples.translation: The reason I was late is because the train was delayed.

examples.sentence: この部屋が汚いのは、掃除をしなかったというのだ。
examples.romanization: Kono heya ga kitanai no wa, souji o shinakatta to iu no da.
examples.translation: The reason this room is dirty is because I didn't clean it.

examples.sentence: 彼女が怒っているのは、彼が約束を破ったというのだ。
examples.romanization: Kanojo ga okotte iru no wa, kare ga yakusoku o yabutta to iu no da.
examples.translation: The reason she is angry is that he broke his promise.

examples.sentence: 彼が成功したのは、努力して勉強したというのだ。
examples.romanization: Kare ga seikou shita no wa, doryoku shite benkyou shita to iu no da.
examples.translation: The reason he succeeded is because he studied hard.

title: ～というのは (〜to iu no wa)
shortExplanation: Used to provide an explanation or definition; 'that is to say...', 'by that, I mean...'.
longExplanation: The ～というのは grammar point is used to provide an explanation or definition of the preceding statement or word. It can be translated as 'that is to say...', 'by that, I mean...', or 'what I mean by...'.

examples.sentence: 日本に行くというのは、日本に旅行することです。
examples.romanization: Nihon ni iku to iu no wa, Nihon ni ryokou suru koto desu.
examples.translation: Going to Japan, that is to say, traveling to Japan.

examples.sentence: この問題は難しいというのは、解決に時間がかかるということです。
examples.romanization: Kono mondai wa muzukashii to iu no wa, kaiketsu ni jikan ga kakaru to iu koto desu.
examples.translation: When I say this problem is difficult, I mean it takes time to solve.

examples.sentence: 彼が怒っているというのは、彼が不満を感じているということです。
examples.romanization: Kare ga okotteiru to iu no wa, kare ga fuman wo kanjiteiru to iu koto desu.
examples.translation: By saying that he's angry, I mean he's feeling dissatisfied.

examples.sentence: 太るというのは、体重が増えるということです。
examples.romanization: Futoru to iu no wa, taijuu ga fueru to iu koto desu.
examples.translation: Gaining weight, that is to say, increasing one's body weight.

title: ～というより (〜to iu yori)
shortExplanation: Express a comparison with preference; 'rather than', 'more like', 'instead of'.
longExplanation: The ～というより grammar point is used to express a comparison where one description is more accurate than another. Translated as 'rather than', 'more like', or 'instead of'.
formation: Verb-casual + というより, い-Adjective + というより, な-Adjective + だというより, Noun + だというより

examples.sentence: この部屋は狭いというより、居心地がいい。
examples.romanization: Kono heya wa semai to iu yori, igokochi ga ii.
examples.translation: Rather than saying this room is small, it's more like it's cozy.

examples.sentence: 彼は怖いというより、頼りがいがある。
examples.romanization: Kare wa kowai to iu yori, tayori gai ga aru.
examples.translation: Instead of saying he's scary, he's more like a reliable person.

examples.sentence: 映画はつまらないというより、ちょっと長かった。
examples.romanization: Eiga wa tsumaranai to iu yori, chotto nagakatta.
examples.translation: Rather than calling the movie boring, I'd say it was a bit long.

examples.sentence: 彼女は友達だというより、家族のような存在だ。
examples.romanization: Kanojo wa tomodachi da to iu yori, kazoku no you na sonzai da.
examples.translation: Rather than a friend, she's more like family.

title: ～といっても (〜to ittemo)
longExplanation: The ～といっても grammar point is used to show a contrast or clarify that 'even though' something is the case, it does not necessarily lead to the expected result. It can be translated as 'even though', 'although', or 'but'.
formation: Verb-casual + といっても, い-Adjective + といっても, な-Adjective + だといっても, Noun + だといっても

examples.sentence: 彼は有名だといっても、みんなに知られているわけではありません。
examples.romanization: Kare wa yuumei da to ittemo, minna ni shirarete iru wake de wa arimasen.
examples.translation: Even though he's famous, it doesn't mean everyone knows him.

examples.sentence: このスープは辛いといっても、私にはちょうどいいです。
examples.romanization: Kono suupu wa karai to ittemo, watashi ni wa choudo ii desu.
examples.translation: Although this soup is spicy, it's just right for me.

examples.sentence: 彼女は若いですが、経験があるといっても、まだ新人です。
examples.romanization: Kanojo wa wakai desu ga, keiken ga aru to ittemo, mada shinjin desu.
examples.translation: She's young, and although she has some experience, she's still a newcomer.

examples.sentence: このレストランは高いだといっても、美味しい料理が食べられるので価値があります。
examples.romanization: Kono resutoran wa takai da to ittemo, oishii ryouri ga taberareru node kachi ga arimasu.
examples.translation: Even though this restaurant is expensive, it's worth it because you can enjoy delicious dishes.

title: ～とおり (〜toori)
shortExplanation: Expresses that something is done 'as is', 'as stated', or 'as instructed'.
longExplanation: The ～とおり grammar point is used to express that something is done exactly as stated, instructed, or shown. It is commonly used with verbs and nouns, and can be translated as 'just like', 'as per', or 'according to'.
formation: Verb-て form + とおり, Noun + のとおり

examples.sentence: 先生が言ったとおり、宿題をやりました。
examples.romanization: Sensei ga itta toori, shukudai wo yarimashita.
examples.translation: I did my homework exactly as the teacher said.

examples.sentence: 地図に書いてあるとおりに行けば、駅に着きます。
examples.romanization: Chizu ni kaite aru toori ni ikeba, eki ni tsukimasu.
examples.translation: If you follow what's written on the map, you'll arrive at the station.

examples.sentence: レシピのとおりにケーキを作った。
examples.romanization: Reshipi no toori ni keeki o tsukutta.
examples.translation: I baked the cake according to the recipe.

examples.sentence: 彼女は約束したとおりに時間通りに来ました。
examples.romanization: Kanojo wa yakusoku shita toori ni jikan doori ni kimashita.
examples.translation: She arrived on time, just as she promised.

title: ～とく (〜toku)
shortExplanation: Express doing something in advance or for future convenience (casual form of ～ておく).
longExplanation: The ～とく grammar point (from ～ておく) is used to express doing something in advance or preparing for something. It implies you're performing an action now to avoid inconvenience later. It is a casual, colloquial contraction of ～ておく.
formation: Verb-て form + とく (e.g., 食べておく→食べとく, 読んでおく→読んどく)

examples.sentence: 夜遅くなるから、今晩のご飯を作っとく。
examples.romanization: Yoru osoku naru kara, konban no gohan wo tsukutoku.
examples.translation: Since it will be late tonight, I'll prepare dinner in advance.

examples.sentence: 傘が必要かもしれないので、持っておく。
examples.romanization: Kasa ga hitsuyou kamoshirenai node, motte oku.
examples.translation: I might need an umbrella, so I'll bring one along (just in case).

examples.sentence: 試験が近いから、今から勉強しとこう。
examples.romanization: Shiken ga chikai kara, ima kara benkyou shitokou.
examples.translation: The exam is coming up, so I'll start studying now.

examples.sentence: 明日は忙しいので、洗濯をしとく。
examples.romanization: Ashita wa isogashii node, sentaku wo shitoku.
examples.translation: Since I'll be busy tomorrow, I'll do the laundry in advance.

title: ～ところが (〜tokoro ga)
shortExplanation: Expresses a contrast or unexpected outcome; 'however', 'but', 'even though'.
longExplanation: The ～ところが grammar point is used to express a contrast or an unexpected outcome. It can be translated as 'however', 'but', or 'even though' in English. It emphasizes a situation that contradicts what was expected.
formation: Phrase 1 (expected situation) + ところが + Phrase 2 (unexpected result)

examples.sentence: 彼はいつも遅刻するところが、今日は早く来ました。
examples.romanization: Kare wa itsumo chikoku suru tokoro ga, kyou wa hayaku kimashita.
examples.translation: He's always late, but today he arrived early.

examples.sentence: 昨日は暑かったところが、今日は寒くなりました。
examples.romanization: Kinou wa atsukatta tokoro ga, kyou wa samuku narimashita.
examples.translation: Yesterday was hot, but today it got cold.

examples.sentence: 試合で負けると思ったところが、意外にも勝ちました。
examples.romanization: Shiai de makeru to omotta tokoro ga, igai ni mo kachimashita.
examples.translation: I thought we would lose the match, but surprisingly we won.

examples.sentence: 決勝戦で優勝するところが、最後のポイントで負けました。
examples.romanization: Kesshousen de yuushou suru tokoro ga, saigo no pointo de makemashita.
examples.translation: We were about to win the final, but we lost at the last point.

title: ～ところだった (〜tokoro datta)
shortExplanation: Expresses a near miss or a situation that almost happened; 'was just about to', 'almost', 'nearly'.
longExplanation: The ～ところだった grammar point is used to express a situation that almost occurred or something that the speaker was just about to do. It can be translated as 'was just about to', 'almost', or 'nearly' in English. Typically, it is formed with the dictionary form or ている form of a verb + ところだった.
formation: Verb (dictionary form or ている form) + ところだった

examples.sentence: もう少しで遅れるところだった。
examples.romanization: Mou sukoshi de okureru tokoro datta.
examples.translation: I was just about to be late.

examples.sentence: 彼が危うく事故にあうところだった。
examples.romanization: Kare ga ayauku jiko ni au tokoro datta.
examples.translation: He almost had an accident.

examples.sentence: 電車に乗るところだったが、ドアが閉まってしまった。
examples.romanization: Densha ni noru tokoro datta ga, doa ga shimatte shimatta.
examples.translation: I was just about to get on the train, but the door closed.

examples.sentence: 忘れ物をするところだった。
examples.romanization: Wasuremono wo suru tokoro datta.
examples.translation: I almost forgot my belongings.

title: ところで (tokorode)
shortExplanation: Used for changing the topic or bringing up a new topic; 'by the way', 'speaking of'.
longExplanation: The ところで (tokorode) grammar point is used to change the topic of conversation or introduce a new topic. It can be translated as 'by the way' or 'speaking of' in English. It is often used when the speaker wants to ask a question or share some information on a different subject. It can be placed at the beginning or in the middle of a sentence.
formation: ところで + new topic or question

examples.sentence: ところで、昨日の宿題はもう終わりましたか？
examples.romanization: Tokorode, kinou no shukudai wa mou owari mashita ka?
examples.translation: By the way, did you finish yesterday's homework?

examples.sentence: 彼はプールで泳いでいます。ところで、お昼ご飯は何にしますか？
examples.romanization: Kare wa puuru de oyoide imasu. Tokorode, ohiru gohan wa nani ni shimasu ka?
examples.translation: He is swimming in the pool. By the way, what do you want for lunch?

examples.sentence: 昨日は楽しかったですね。ところで、この写真を見ましたか？
examples.romanization: Kinou wa tanoshikatta desu ne. Tokorode, kono shashin wo mimashita ka?
examples.translation: Yesterday was fun, wasn't it? By the way, did you see this photo?

examples.sentence: ところで、明日の会議の時間を知っていますか？
examples.romanization: Tokorode, ashita no kaigi no jikan wo shitte imasu ka?
examples.translation: By the way, do you know the time of tomorrow's meeting?

title: ～としたら (〜to shitara)
longExplanation: The ～としたら grammar point is used to express a hypothetical situation or assumption. It can be translated as 'if', 'suppose', or 'assuming' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
formation: Verb-casual + としたら, い-Adjective + としたら, な-Adjective + だとしたら, Noun + だとしたら

examples.sentence: 明日雨が降るとしたら、傘を持って行きましょう。
examples.romanization: Ashita ame ga furu to shitara, kasa wo motte ikimashou.
examples.translation: If it rains tomorrow, let's bring an umbrella.

examples.sentence: このケーキが美味しくないとしたら、誰も食べないでしょう。
examples.romanization: Kono keeki ga oishikunai to shitara, daremo tabenai deshou.
examples.translation: If this cake is not delicious, nobody will eat it.

examples.sentence: 彼が病気だとしたら、すぐに病院に行かせてあげてください。
examples.romanization: Kare ga byouki da to shitara, sugu ni byouin ni ikasete agete kudasai.
examples.translation: If he is sick, please take him to the hospital right away.

examples.sentence: 彼女が学生だとしたら、このレストランは割引があるでしょう。
examples.romanization: Kanojo ga gakusei da to shitara, kono resutoran wa waribiki ga aru deshou.
examples.translation: If she is a student, there will be a discount at this restaurant.

title: ～として (〜to shite)
shortExplanation: Indicates a role, capacity, or identity; 'as', 'in the capacity of'.
longExplanation: The ～として grammar point is used to express a role, capacity, or identity in which someone or something functions. It can be translated as 'as' or 'in the capacity of' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
formation: Verb-casual + として, い-Adjective + として, な-Adjective + だとして, Noun + だとして

examples.sentence: 彼は弁護士として働いています。
examples.romanization: Kare wa bengoshi to shite hataraite imasu.
examples.translation: He is working as a lawyer.

examples.sentence: この料理はスナックとして食べられます。
examples.romanization: Kono ryouri wa sunakku to shite taberaremasu.
examples.translation: This dish can be eaten as a snack.

examples.sentence: 彼女はリーダーとして尊敬されている。
examples.romanization: Kanojo wa riidaa to shite sonkei sarete iru.
examples.translation: She is respected as a leader.

examples.sentence: この本は参考書として使われます。
examples.romanization: Kono hon wa sankousho to shite tsukawaremasu.
examples.translation: This book is used as a reference.

title: ～どんなに～ことか (〜donna ni〜koto ka)
shortExplanation: Expresses the extent of something or emphasizes the degree of a condition or situation.
longExplanation: The ～どんなに～ことか grammar point is used to emphasize the extent of a condition or circumstance, and to express how much or to what degree something is happening. It is often translated as 'how much', 'how greatly', or 'to what extent' in English. This pattern is usually used with an adjective or verb in a sentence.
formation: どんなに + Adjective + ことか, どんなに + Verb + ことか

examples.sentence: どんなに疲れたことか、言葉では表せません。
examples.romanization: Donna ni tsukareta koto ka, kotoba de wa arawasemasen.
examples.translation: I can't put into words how tired I am.

examples.sentence: どんなに辛いことか、彼女は毎日頑張って働いています。
examples.romanization: Donna ni tsurai koto ka, kanojo wa mainichi ganbatte hataraiteimasu.
examples.translation: How hard it must be, she works hard every day.

examples.sentence: 彼の成功はどんなに喜ばしいことか。
examples.romanization: Kare no seikou wa donna ni yorokobashii koto ka.
examples.translation: How happy his success must be.

examples.sentence: どんなに楽しいことか、みんなで旅行に行く。
examples.romanization: Donna ni tanoshii koto ka, minna de ryokou ni iku.
examples.translation: How fun it is to go on a trip with everyone.

title: どんなに～ても (donna ni ~ temo)
shortExplanation: Expresses 'no matter how much' or 'even if'; emphasizes the degree of a situation.
longExplanation: The どんなに～ても grammar point is used to emphasize the degree of a situation or condition, often translated as 'no matter how much' or 'even if' in English. It can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, and な-adjectives.
formation: どんなに + Verb-てform + も, どんなに + い-Adjective-てform + も, どんなに + な-Adjective + でも

examples.sentence: どんなに勉強しても、まだわからないことがある。
examples.romanization: Donna ni benkyou shite mo, mada wakaranai koto ga aru.
examples.translation: No matter how much I study, there are still things I don't understand.

examples.sentence: どんなに速く走っても、彼には勝てません。
examples.romanization: Donna ni hayaku hashitte mo, kare ni wa katemasen.
examples.translation: No matter how fast I run, I can't beat him.

examples.sentence: どんなに疲れても、仕事を終わらせるまで帰れません。
examples.romanization: Donna ni tsukarete mo, shigoto o owaraseru made kaeremasen.
examples.translation: No matter how tired I am, I can't go home until I finish my work.

examples.sentence: どんなに美味しくても、これ以上食べられない。
examples.romanization: Donna ni oishikute mo, kore ijou taberarenai.
examples.translation: No matter how delicious it is, I can't eat any more.

title: ～ないことはない (〜nai koto wa nai)
shortExplanation: Express the idea that 'it's not that it's impossible' or 'it's not that it cannot be done'.
longExplanation: The ～ないことはない grammar point is used to express that something is not impossible, or not that it cannot be done. It creates a softer, more indirect way of saying that something is possible or can be done, but not necessarily easy or preferred.
formation: Verb-ない form + ことはない

examples.sentence: この問題を解けないことはないが、時間がかかりそうだ。
examples.romanization: Kono mondai wo tokenai koto wa nai ga, jikan ga kakari sou da.
examples.translation: It's not that I can't solve this problem, but it seems like it will take time.

examples.sentence: 彼に会わないことはないけど、あまり話したくない。
examples.romanization: Kare ni awanai koto wa nai kedo, amari hanashitakunai.
examples.translation: It's not that I can't meet him, but I don't really want to talk.

examples.sentence: この映画を見ないことはないけれど、他の映画がもっと面白いと思う。
examples.romanization: Kono eiga wo minai koto wa nai keredo, hoka no eiga ga motto omoshiroi to omou.
examples.translation: It's not that I cannot watch this movie, but I think other movies are more interesting.

examples.sentence: その本を読まないことはないが、長いので気をつけてください。
examples.romanization: Sono hon wo yomanai koto wa nai ga, nagai node ki wo tsukete kudasai.
examples.translation: It's not that I can't read that book, but it's long, so be careful.
